sources.title: Eurostat, Structural business statistics (sbs) — reference metadata (ESMS), section 7, Confidentiality
passages: a cell is confidential if it is primary or secondary confidential.
A cell is primary confidential if the extrapolated number of contributors is positive but less than a specified number that is referred to as the "minimum threshold".
a well-informed intruder, i.e., the second largest contributor, can estimate the value of the largest contributor within a chosen percentage, p%, of the true value of the largest contributor.
A cell is secondary confidential if it can be used with marginal totals to disclose primary confidential cells.
The thresholds are defined for each country.

sources.title: Eurostat, Structural business statistics — national reference metadata, Estonia, section 7
passages: The data have to be classified into groups of at least three persons (primary confidentiality — too few enterprises)
x denotes dominance limit in Statistics Estonia and its value is confidential
As Estonia is a small country the rate of confidential cells is considerable.
The rate of confidential cells_Annexes I to IV_2020 (%) ... SBSCP_1A 13,0 0,0 13,3 16,4 11,6 (columns: TOTAL, Section, Division, Group, Class)

sources.title: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 on European statistics, Article 3(7), Official Journal text as adopted
passages: 'confidential data' means data which allow statistical units to be identified, either directly or indirectly, thereby disclosing individual information.

passages: Number of enterprises non confidential, if number of employments is confidential (field label, every report)

prior_art: Eurostat's national SBS metadata pages publish a 'rate of confidential cells' per dataset and activity level (Estonia's, opened). The per-country rate is therefore a quantity the producers already report, page by page, under their own definitions. Not found so far: a cross-country comparison of those rates, or the relation of withholding to the number of enterprises measured on the disseminated table. Searched: two web searches and the Eurostat metadata; the official-statistics journals have not been searched directly. 2026-10-25 (session 231): the national reports' fixed field on whether the firm count stays public was set against the disseminated table, state by state; no earlier comparison of declared against practised count suppression was found. The house's paper index (1,158 entries, fetched 2026-10-25) returns zero for confidential, disclosure, suppress, official statistic and Eurostat, and one further web search found none.
